name: Bifida ferment lysate
lead: Bifida ferment lysate (BFL) is a cosmetic ingredient obtained by fermenting Bifidobacterium and then breaking down (lysing) the cells and extracting the result. It is used in repair and barrier serums as a 'probiotic' or postbiotic active [1].

Researchers describe semi-active or inactive probiotics and their extracts as having properties that may soothe irritated skin and support the skin barrier, and Bifidobacterium has been studied for acne and atopic dermatitis [1]. Under the 2021 ISAPP definition, a postbiotic is a preparation of inanimate microorganisms or their components that confers a health benefit; Wikipedia notes postbiotic research is emerging and needs confirmation in well-designed human studies [5].
Evidence specific to BFL for appearance outcomes consists of laboratory work and a few clinical studies of multi-ingredient products.

paras: BFL appears in serums, creams and sheet masks marketed for barrier repair, calming and anti-aging. A DailyMed-listed topical essence, for example, pairs it with rice extract, ceramide, collagen and tocopherol [6].
A 2023 in vitro study reported that BFL reinforced skin-barrier function and helped maintain homeostasis of skin defenses in cell models [1].

A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled multicentre study evaluated a class IIa medical device for mild-to-moderate acne that contained lactic acid, azelaic acid/polyglyceryl-3 copolymer, azelamidopropyl dimethyl amine and bifida ferment lysate [2]. Because it was a combination product, effects cannot be assigned to BFL itself.

A randomized controlled design studied three facial sheet-mask types (pure water, hyaluronan and bifida ferment lysate) worn for different durations, measuring skin reactions and stratum corneum changes, and noting that prolonged mask use may cause skin inflammation [3]. A 2026 multicenter investigation tested day and night antioxidant serums for sensitive skin, with BFL among the night-serum ingredients alongside other actives [4].
No serious adverse events specific to BFL were identified in the sources reviewed. Product labels list standard external-use warnings such as avoiding contact with eyes [6].

card.summary: Probiotic-derived ferment in repair serums, with lab barrier data and only combination-product trials.
card.note: Human studies used multi-ingredient products, so BFL's own effect is unclear.

quick.overview:
BFL comes from fermented, broken-down Bifidobacterium and is added to serums for barrier repair and soothing.

Lab studies are positive in cell models, while human studies tested combination products.
quick.mechanism: A 2023 cell study reported strengthened barrier function and stable skin defense signalling. How this translates to human skin is not established.
quick.risks: No specific harms were found in the reviewed sources. It is a cosmetic ingredient rather than a drug, and prolonged sheet-mask wear has been linked to skin irritation generally.
